2 credentialing requirement which states that all students need a master’s degree with experiential learning to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists (RDNs).
Until 2024, a BS degree and an internship that provides experiential learning are required to become a RDN.
This change prompted free-standing internships to partner with universities to meet this new degree requirement.
The University of Rhode Island has successfully worked with Sodexo to provide a master’s degree to its interns for the past 6 years.
We are now formalizing the existing partnership with Sodexo by becoming an accredited Future Graduate Program to meet the Future Education Model (FEM) Standards as outlined by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND).
The FEM requires enhanced integration between the didactic and experiential components as part of the accreditation.
Curriculum changes to meet the new standards were approved in the spring of 2021.
The FEM Program will begin in the fall of 2022.
Students who complete these requirements need to be in a separate track to best manage our accreditation.
In 2018, URI expanded the master’s degree offering to RDNs employed by Sodexo.

This program was requested by Sodexo to help their current RDNs to remain competitive with new graduates entering the workforce with master’s degrees.
RDNs complete the MS degree in a separate cohort, and complete individualized learning experiences instead of the standard experiential learning rotations.
We are requesting a second non-accredited track in the MS in Dietetics degree to allow us to continue to offer the program to these students and to students who are unable to complete the accredited track.
The MS in Dietetics has graduated 217 students as of December 2021.

What are the learning goals (what students are expected to gain, achieve, know, or demonstrate by completion of the program)?

Goal #1- The Future Graduate Program will prepare graduates from diverse backgrounds to become Registered Dietitian Nutritionists who will promote and advance the profession of dietetics. a) At least 80% of program graduates complete program/degree requirements within 2 years (150% of the program length). b) At least 90 percent of program graduates take the CDR credentialing exam for dietitian nutritionists within 12 months of program completion. c) The program’s one-year pass rate (graduates who pass the registration exam within one year of first attempt) on the CDR credentialing exam for dietitian nutritionists is at least 80%. d) Of those who complete a survey one-year post graduation, 25% of graduates will show activities that promote and advance the field of nutrition and dietetics. e) At least 10% of graduates will be from diverse backgrounds.

Goal #2- The Future Graduate Program will prepare graduates will be highly competent practitioners with expertise in medical nutrition therapy, community nutrition, foodservice management, leadership, and research. a) Of those who complete a survey upon program completion, 75% of graduates will rate their knowledge and practice skills as ‘above average’ or ‘excellent’ in medical nutrition therapy, community nutrition, foodservice management, leadership, and research. b) Of graduates who seek employment, 75% percent are employed in nutrition and dietetics or related fields within 12 months of graduation. c) Of those returning surveys, 75% percent of employers will rate graduates ‘above average’ or ‘excellent’ in their knowledge and practice skills in medical nutrition therapy, community nutrition, foodservice management, leadership, and research.
